CLM1499455592016-01-1320Attorney Docket No. 11541-0039-01000WHAT IS CLAIMED IS:
1. A computer-implemented method of assessment of visceral ischemia and related disorders, the method comprising: receiving a patient-specific anatomic model of a patient's visceral vasculature, including visceral vasculature of the patient's visceral organs and bowel; determining a location in the patient-specific anatomic model of the patient's visceral vasculature; determining, for the location in the patient-specific anatomic model, a blood flow characteristic defining a characteristic of blood flow through the location in the patient- specific anatomic model of the patient's visceral vasculature; determining a tissue region of the patient's bowel distal to the location in the patient-specific anatomic model of the patient's visceral vasculature; and generating an assessment of blood supply adequacy defining an adequacy of blood supply to the tissue region of the patient's viscera or bowel, or generating a risk score defining a risk of disease of the patient's viscera or bowel, based on the determined blood flow characteristic and an expected blood flow characteristic associated with the tissue region of the patient's bowel.Independent
2. The computer-implemented method of claim 1, wherein the blood flow characteristic includes one or more of blood pressure, flow rate, fractional flow reserve, or portal venous pressure.Dependent
3. The computer-implemented method of claim 1, further comprising:24Attorney Docket No. 11541-0039-01000receiving the patient-specific anatomic model including at least a portion of the patient's bowel; determining blood flow demand based on a received physiological state and the portion of the patient's bowel; and determining the assessment of blood supply adequacy based on the determined blood flow demand and the determined blood flow characteristic at the location in the patient-specific model of the patient's visceral vasculature.Dependent
4. The computer-implemented method of claim 3, further including: subdividing the patient-specific anatomic model comprising the portion of the patient's bowel into one or more bowel regions; determining an association between a vessel of the patient's visceral vasculature and at least one bowel region of the one or more bowel regions; and determining blood flow adequacy for one or more locations of the a portion of the patient's bowel distal to the at least one bowel region, based on the determined blood flow adequacy for the at least one bowel region.Dependent
5. The computer-implemented method of claim 1, further comprising: determining the blood flow characteristic at the location of the patient-specific anatomic model of the patient's visceral vasculature using a fluid simulation or blood flow characteristics associated with one or more other patients.25Attorney Docket No. 11541-0039-01000Dependent
6. The computer-implemented method of claim 1, further comprising: receiving a physiological state associated with the patient; and generating the assessment of blood supply adequacy to the patient's bowl or generating the risk score for risk of disease for the patient's viscera or bowel, further based on the received physiological state.Dependent
7. The computer-implemented method of claim 6, further comprising: modifying a geometry of the patient-specific anatomic model or modifying the received physiological state of the patient; determining a blood flow characteristic at a location in the patient-specific anatomic model of the patient's visceral vasculature based on the modified patient- specific anatomic model or modified physiological state of the patient; and generating an updated assessment of blood supply adequacy to the patient's viscera or bowel or generating a risk score for risk of disease to one or more regions of the patient's viscera or bowel, based on the determined blood flow characteristic at a location in the patient-specific anatomic model of the patient's visceral vasculature based on the modified patient-specific anatomic model or modified physiological state of the patient.Dependent
8. The computer-implemented method of claim 1, further comprising: determining the risk score for risk of disease to one or more regions of the patient's viscera or bowel based on the assessment of blood supply adequacy to the patient's viscera or bowel, wherein the risk of disease may include risk of one or more of26Attorney Docket No. 11541-0039-01000mesenteric ischemia, intestinal ischemia, ischemic colitis, abdominal pain, gangrene, bowel perforation, sepsis, stricture, mesenteric ischemia, inflammatory conditions.Dependent
9. A system for assessment of visceral ischemia and related disorders, the system comprising: a data storage device storing instructions for assessment of ischemic colitis; and a processor configured to execute the instructions to perform a method including: receiving a patient-specific anatomic model of a patient's visceral vasculature, including visceral vasculature of the patient's visceral organs and bowel; determining a location in the patient-specific anatomic model of the patient's visceral vasculature; determining, for the location in the patient-specific anatomic model, a blood flow characteristic defining a characteristic of blood flow through the location in the patient-specific anatomic model of the patient's visceral vasculature; determining a tissue region of the patient's bowel distal to the location in the patient-specific anatomic model of the patient's visceral vasculature; and generating an assessment of blood supply adequacy defining an adequacy of blood supply to the tissue region of the patient's viscera or bowel, or generating a risk score defining a risk of disease of the patient's viscera or bowel, based on the determined blood flow characteristic and an expected blood flow characteristic associated with the tissue region of the patient's bowel.27Attorney Docket No. 11541-0039-01000Independent
10. The system of claim 9, wherein the blood flow characteristic includes one or more of blood pressure, flow rate, fractional flow reserve, or portal venous pressure.Dependent
11. The system of claim 9, wherein the system is further configured for: receiving the patient-specific anatomic model including at least a portion of the patient's bowel; determining blood flow demand based on a received physiological state and the portion of the patient's bowel; and determining the assessment of blood supply adequacy based on the determined blood flow demand and the determined blood flow characteristic at the location in the patient-specific model of the patient's visceral vasculature.Dependent
12. The system of claim 11, wherein the system is further configured for: subdividing the patient-specific anatomic model comprising the portion of the patient's bowel into one or more bowel regions; determining an association between a vessel of the patient's visceral vasculature and at least one bowel region of the one or more bowel regions; and determining blood flow adequacy for one or more locations of the a portion of the patient's bowel distal to the at least one bowel region, based on the determined blood flow adequacy for the at least one bowel region.Dependent
13. 14. 15. 17. 20. The non-transitory computer readable medium of claim 19, the method further comprising: subdividing the patient-specific anatomic model comprising the portion of the patient's bowel into one or more bowel regions; determining an association between a vessel of the patient's visceral vasculature and at least one bowel region of the one or more bowel regions; and31Attorney Docket No. 11541-0039-01000determining blood flow adequacy for one or more locations of the a portion of the patient's bowel distal to the at least one bowel region, based on the determined blood flow adequacy for the at least one bowel region.32Dependent
